One token layer: SystemSketch wears light, dark, Obsidian, and Dark Modern

The chrome was authored light-only — 625 colour literals across the chrome stylesheets at be53803. It now names 618 tokens from one closed vocabulary and holds 4 literals (the four quick-colour swatches, marked as shape-colour content), and a theme is a table of values: the default is derived from tldraw's own palette so the board and the panels on it cannot disagree, a host theme reads the IDE's live variables, and a palette — Obsidian's two, VS Code's Dark Modern, or any theme file a person imports — arrives inline and is pushed back into tldraw's own menus. Legibility is a measured contrast ratio in a real browser, not a screenshot review, and the journey was mutation-tested red.

1 · The design: three layers, and the middle one is the whole idea

Two things in the drawing are load-bearing. The default theme's block is declared on .tl-container, not on the app root: a custom property is substituted where it is declared, and --tl-* exists only from the container down — declared any higher, every var(--tl-…) resolves to nothing and the chrome inherits that nothing. And every theme other than the default is pushed back into --tl-color-panel, --tl-color-text-1, --tl-color-divider and friends on the same container, which is why tldraw's own context menu, dialogs and zoom controls wear Dark Modern too rather than sitting beside it in tldraw-dark.

The root also carries a fallback in :where() — tldraw's own light and dark values, copied — so the embed lane's strips outside the container paint correctly and a host nobody has written a block for gets a correct-looking app. resolveHostTheme() maps an unknown host to systemsketch first; the CSS fallback is the second line, not the first. Adding Obsidian's plugin is the obsidian block that already exists plus the string 'obsidian' in KNOWN_HOST_THEMES; the gate test checks both are present.

The vocabulary

TokenWhat it names
--ss-surfacethe pane behind everything — the canvas
--ss-surface-raiseda panel, popout, menu or toolbar sitting on it
--ss-surface-sunkenan input, a well, a resting chip
--ss-surface-hoverpointer feedback on a transparent control
--ss-surface-activepointer feedback on a chip, or a pressed state
--ss-surface-inversea floating pill in the opposite polarity
--ss-textprimary copy
--ss-text-mutedsecondary copy, eyebrows, labels
--ss-text-faintplaceholders and disabled copy — never body text
--ss-text-inversecopy on --ss-surface-inverse
--ss-bordera divider
--ss-accentselection and focus
--ss-accent-textlegible text on --ss-accent
--ss-dangera destructive state
--ss-warninga cautionary state
--ss-successa confirmed state
--ss-code-surfacethe well a code sample sits in
--ss-code-textthe ink of that sample
--ss-shadow-1a resting panel
--ss-shadow-2a floating one

Derived, never per-theme: --ss-border-strong, --ss-border-inverse, --ss-surface-inverse-hover, --ss-accent-hover, --ss-accent-soft, --ss-accent-soft-hover. One rule the measurements forced: --ss-accent-soft is a surface, and copy on it is --ss-text, never --ss-accent — see §4.

3 · The gate: contrast, measured

For every piece of chrome that carries text or an icon the journey reads the painted foreground and the effective background off the live element — compositing translucent layers down to the first opaque one — and computes the WCAG ratio. Body text needs 4.5:1; text on an accent fill, icons and input boundaries 3:1. The six tightest readings across all themes:

4 · What the oracle found that a screenshot review would not

  • Accent-coloured copy on an accent-tinted chip cannot reach 4.5:1 in any palette. Measured 2.60 (Dark Modern), 2.83 (Obsidian Dark), 2.91 (tldraw light), 3.01 (Obsidian Light), 4.29 (tldraw dark) on the settings rail's active item — and the same pattern sat on the tool menu, the depth navigator, the inspector's count pill and icon picker, and the dev panel. All of them now paint ink on the tint and mark the active state with a 3px accent bar or ring; the rule is written into tokens.css.
  • tldraw's text-3 on its low surface is 4.14:1 in light — tuned for its panel (4.62), not for a chip. The default theme derives --ss-text-muted as color-mix(text-3 88%, text-1), which clears 4.5 on every surface the chrome uses without touching tldraw.
  • An input outline at 45% ink measured 2.5–2.9:1 in the light themes; 55% clears 3:1 in all five.
  • Four phantom variables were resolving to their fallbacks all along: --tl-color-text-2 (8 uses; tldraw has text-0, -1, -3), --tl-font-ui (3), and unprefixed --color-panel / --color-text-3 in the Block picker and the workspace title. The gate now asserts every --tl-* a stylesheet reads exists in tldraw.css.

5 · Where every value came from

Dark Modern — read from the theme file Cursor ships

/**
 * Dark Modern — a VS Code colour theme as a SystemSketch palette.
 *
 * GENERATED by scripts/import_vscode_theme.mjs — do not edit by hand.
 *
 * Read from, outermost first (each file overrides the one it includes):
 *   ../../../../../../usr/share/cursor/resources/app/extensions/theme-defaults/themes/dark_modern.json (sha256 e6a39ef275a3)
 *   ../../../../../../usr/share/cursor/resources/app/extensions/theme-defaults/themes/dark_plus.json (sha256 88f5b662378c)
 *   ../../../../../../usr/share/cursor/resources/app/extensions/theme-defaults/themes/dark_vs.json (sha256 d1b5e8ff4101)
 * Colours in the merged table: 139.
 * Tokens no layer named, painted from VS Code's defaults: surfaceHover, surfaceActive, warning, shadow1.

scripts/import_vscode_theme.mjs resolves the include chain the way VS Code does (deepest first, outermost overrides) and hands the merged table to the same vsCodeThemeTokens() the Settings dialog runs on an imported file — one mapping, two callers. Cursor's workbench.colorTheme is Default Dark Modern, so this is the palette Zach sees in his editor. tests/test_theme_tokens.py re-hashes the installed files and fails if they have moved since the palette was generated.

Obsidian Light and Dark — read from Obsidian's own app.css

/**
 * Obsidian's default theme as two SystemSketch palettes.
 *
 * GENERATED by scripts/extract_obsidian_palette.py — do not edit by hand.
 *
 * Read from Obsidian 1.13.7 (/home/bam/.config/obsidian/obsidian-1.13.7.asar), app.css sha256 f612f1e8f364.
 * Each variable is the one the [data-ss-theme='obsidian'] host block in
 * tokens.css reads, resolved through Obsidian's own cascade to a literal, so
 * a board looks the same hosted in Obsidian and merely wearing its look.

scripts/extract_obsidian_palette.py pulls app.css out of the asar, merges the top-level body, .theme-light and .theme-dark blocks the way the cascade would, and resolves each variable the [data-ss-theme='obsidian'] host block reads — the names come from tokens.css itself, so the live-Obsidian mapping and the standalone palette cannot name different variables. The accent is Obsidian's own hsl(calc(var(--accent-h) − 1), …) chain, evaluated.

6 · The VS Code plugin: the board follows the workbench

The journey's pin — painted: false, “the board stays light on purpose” — is now painted: workbenchIsDark, and two things are read that were not before: the canvas colour must equal the workbench's own --vscode-editor-background as the webview receives it, and the inspector's copy is measured as a ratio on the very element that used to render invisible.

  • VS Code: the workbench theme reaches the board — .monaco-workbench paints rgb(37, 37, 38), the canvas records "dark", tldraw paints dark (rgb(18, 19, 20) = the workbench's editor.background #121314), and the chrome wears the "vscode" theme
  • VS Code: the inspector is legible in the dark workbench — section-title 4.8:1, field > span 4.8:1, tabs > [role="tab"].is-active 9.48:1
  • Cursor: the workbench theme reaches the board — .monaco-workbench paints rgb(37, 37, 38), the canvas records "dark", tldraw paints dark (rgb(24, 24, 24) = the workbench's editor.background #181818), and the chrome wears the "vscode" theme
  • Cursor: the inspector is legible in the dark workbench — section-title 8.3:1, field > span 8.3:1, tabs > [role="tab"].is-active 14.82:1

A detail worth knowing: the editor background a webview is handed is not always the theme's editor.background — VS Code's fresh profile reported #121314 and Cursor's #181818. The canvas is painted with whatever the host says, which is the point.

8 · Decision surface

Done and proved — everything above, with npm run check green (18 new vitest tests, 13 new Python gate tests), the five-theme contrast journey green and mutation-tested, and both IDE journeys re-run against the packaged VSIX.

Left, and next rather than blocked

  • src/appearance/appearance.css is the one chrome file still on literals, deliberately: it is the FigJam appearance pill the appearance track is actively editing (its values equal --ss-surface-inverse / --ss-text-inverse), and a merge conflict there would cost more than a week on the allowlist. Pointing it at those two tokens is a ten-line change once that track lands.
  • The obsidian host block is verified against Obsidian's stylesheet, not a running Obsidian — there is no Obsidian plugin yet to run it in. The standalone Obsidian palettes are the same variables resolved, so the day the plugin exists the check is one journey.
  • Syntax colours: an imported theme's tokenColors are carried on the record untouched. SystemSketch renders no syntax highlighting today, so --ss-code-surface / --ss-code-text (the notes editor, port types) are what “code wears the theme” means for now.

Needs Zach — each with the default that holds if he says nothing

  • One accent, taken from tldraw's selection blue. The old chrome mixed a violet (#7253df) for settings and depth, an indigo (#536dfe) for the toolbar, and a purple Share button. The work order asked for the accent to derive from --tl-color-selected, so the default theme is now one blue everywhere; Obsidian keeps its purple, Dark Modern its #0078d4. Default: keep. If the violet identity mattered, it is one line in the systemsketch block.
  • The selection pill stays dark in dark themes. FigJam, Obsidian and VS Code all keep that pill dark; only tldraw's tooltip flips to white. Default: keep dark; flipping is one token.
  • A labelled button's border is decorative. The journey measures input boundaries at 3:1 and leaves button borders at the hairline the sources use (Dark Modern's own buttons are #FFFFFF12). Default: keep.

Deliberately not done — the Obsidian plugin itself (the work order's increment 4 is “when its plugin exists”); a second copy of tldraw's palette (every default value is derived); and any theming of document content — a Block's port colours and the FigJam swatches render identically in every theme, and the gate exempts exactly those files.
